title: S. Korean Life Expectancy Up 12 Years Since 1990
paragraphs: People in South Korea are living much longer than they did a few decades ago. According to a new study, life expectancy in South Korea has risen by nearly 12 years since 1990.

The study was led by Professor Kang Ji-seung of Korea University and Professor Yon Dong-keon of Kyung Hee University, and it was published in the journal Nature in July 2026. The researchers used data from the Global Burden of Disease study to look at how life expectancy changed in 34 Asian countries and regions between 1990 and 2023.

According to the study, the life expectancy of a baby born in South Korea rose from 71.7 years in 1990 to 83.4 years in 2023. This was the third-highest figure among the places studied, after Singapore, at 85.4 years, and Japan, at 84.1 years.

In 2023, women in South Korea had a life expectancy of 86.1 years, while men had a life expectancy of 80.6 years. However, men's life expectancy has risen faster. Since 1990, it has increased by 13.1 years, compared with 10.1 years for women.

What caused the increase? In South Korea and other wealthy places in Asia, the biggest reason was a fall in deaths from heart and blood vessel diseases. In South Asia and Southeast Asia, it was mainly fewer deaths from diarrhea and tuberculosis. South Asia had the biggest rise of all, from 58.6 years to 71.2 years.
However, there were also some worrying findings. The researchers found that high blood pressure, air pollution and poor diets were the main risks that shortened people's lives in Asia.
The researchers said that wealthy countries such as South Korea should do more to prevent disease, for example by controlling high blood pressure, reducing smoking and improving air quality.
